summary:
Project TERRA-NOVA is an interactive mission catalog and assessment system that identifies the best analog location on Earth for various NASA targets in lunar or Martian exploration programs. Using data obtained from satellite telemetry from NASA Moon Trek (LOLA DEM, CE-2 CCD Slope) and Mars Trek (MGS MOLA DEM), I assessed three major scenarios for space missions: the extraction of polar ice in the Shackleton Crater, building of radiation-shielded habitats in Lunar Lava Tubes, and astrobiology and ISRU in Jezero Crater, and matched them with Pingualuit Crater (Canada), Cueva de los Verdes (Spain), and the Río Tinto Basin (Spain).

In order to evaluate the scenario objectively, I evaluated each combination using a weighted Analog Match Score (Topography, Geology, Environment, and Field Utility) and the "What is similar?/How is it similar?/ What is different?" analysis. This system is essential since no Earth analog matches 100% of the conditions in space; however, knowing both advantages and disadvantages (for example, 1G gravity or cryogenic temperatures gap) allows engineers to test equipment before using it for humans.
details:
Project TERRA-NOVA is an interactive mission planning catalog and scoring simulation that pairs NASA’s top priority space explorations targets (lunar and Martian) with validated Earth analog locations. You can analyze three mission scenarios via "What is similar / How is it similar / What is different" approach and run custom space-Earth comparisons using our Analog Match Simulator:

1. Lunar South Pole Ice Extraction Mission: Shackleton Crater (Moon) vs Pingualuit Crater (Nunavik, Canada) with an Analog Match Score 8.5 out of 10.

2. Lunar Subsurface Radiation Shielded Habitats: Lunar Lava Tubes (Marius Hills Pit) vs Cueva de los Verdes (Lanzarote, Spain) with an Analog Match Score 9.0 out of 10.

3. Martian Astrobiology and ISRU Operations: Jezero Crater (Mars) vs Río Tinto Basin (Huelva, Spain) also with aa Analog Match Score 8.8 out of 10.

Criteria considered and scientific methodology

Instead of blindly believing that any location on Earth is an exact replica of space, I developed a weighted Analog Match Score (AMS) with points from 1 to 10 based on evaluating four important criteria such as: topography and relief (30%), geology and soil composition (30%), environmental and thermal conditions (20%) and not least field testing capability (20%). This scoring approach specifically downweights planetary differences like Earth's 1G gravity, breathable atmosphere, abundance of liquid water , and the temperature gap between arctic -40°C and lunar cryogenic -173°C conditions so engineers know exactly which systems each site can reliably validate.

Field testing on Earth dramatically reduces mission risk and cost before launching hardware to the Moon or Mars. By pairing real NASA orbital telemetry with accessible terrestrial sites, Project TERRA-NOVA helps mission planners, engineers, and students quickly identify where to test rover slope traction, subterranean wireless communications, inflatable habitats, and In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) drilling rigs.

Tools, data and software used

Planetary data and Telemetry: NASA Moon Trek (LOLA DEM elevation profiles, CE-2 CCD Slope maps) and NASA Mars Trek (MGS MOLA DEM elevation data).

Visual Presentation: Canva

Interactive Web Application: Base44 for website
